findings.title: Route param name mismatch breaks add_members / remove_member endpoints
findings.body: `add_members` (line 66) and `remove_member` (line 85) call `params.require(:group_id)`, but the routes added in `config/routes.rb` (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` / `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`) are declared directly inside the `resources :groups do ... end` block without a `member do` wrapper or a custom `param:` option. Rails treats such bare routes as member routes using the resource's default id parameter, i.e. `:id` (same as `/admin/groups/:id`), not `:group_id`. As a result the real request path produces `params[:id]`, and `params.require(:group_id)` will raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` for every real HTTP request made by the JS model's `addMembers`/`removeMember` calls (`Discourse.ajax('/admin/groups/' + this.get('id') + '/members.json', ...)`), making the core feature of this PR (adding/removing group members from the admin UI) non-functional in production.

findings.title: Controller specs bypass routing and hide the group_id/id param mismatch
findings.body: The `.add_members` and `.remove_member` specs invoke the controller actions directly with `group_id: ...` (e.g. `xhr :put, :add_members, group_id: 1, usernames: "l77t"`). Rails' `ActionController::TestCase` dispatch bypasses real route recognition and just merges the given params, so these tests pass even though the actual routes (declared without a `member do` wrapper) would supply `:id` instead of `:group_id`. There is no request/integration spec exercising the real route, so the runtime `ParameterMissing` bug described separately is not caught by this test suite.

findings.title: Off-by-one in totalPages causes a phantom empty last page
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100 users with limit 50), this yields 3 instead of the correct 2 pages. Combined with the `next` action's offset calculation (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), clicking "next" from the last real page (offset 50) will set offset to 100 and reload, returning zero members (since indices 0-99 are exhausted) while `currentPage`/`totalPages` both report page 3 of 3, presenting a bogus empty page to the admin instead of correctly computing `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}` likely uses wrong option name
findings.body: The each-helper option for specifying a custom per-item view class in this version of Ember/Handlebars is `itemViewClass`, not `itemView` (as used consistently elsewhere in Discourse, e.g. `itemViewClass="..."`). Using `itemView` means the newly added `group-member` view/template (which renders the avatar, username and the remove-member link) will likely never be applied, so the admin group members list will not render as intended and the "remove member" UI added by this PR may simply not appear.

findings.title: `{{#unless automatic}}` resolves against the wrong context, always showing remove link
findings.body: This template is rendered as the item view for each member inside `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`. Inside that per-item context, `automatic` is looked up on the member (a User) object, not on the outer group/controller, so it will always be undefined/false. Consequently `{{#unless automatic}}` always evaluates true and the "remove member" link is shown even for automatic groups, whose members cannot actually be removed (the server rejects such requests with a 422). This creates a confusing dead-end UI action instead of correctly hiding the control for automatic groups.

findings.title: Public group members page silently truncates to 50 members with no pagination UI
findings.body: `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members` now always paginates with a default `limit` of 50 for every group (previously only automatic groups were capped, at 200, and regular groups returned the full member list). The public-facing `group/members.hbs` template has no next/previous controls (unlike the admin `group.hbs` template, which does), so any group with more than 50 members will silently show only the first 50 with no way to view the rest — a functional regression for larger groups.

findings.title: Controller model changed from members array to Group object without visible controller update
findings.body: Previously `setupController` assigned the resolved members array itself as the controller's `model` (`controller.set('model', this.get('_members'))`), implying the group-members controller is array-oriented, and the template iterated `{{#each m in model}}`. The route now assigns the raw `Group` model object instead (`controller.set("model", model)`) and the template was changed to `{{#each m in members}}`. No controller file for group-members is included in this change set; if the existing controller is an `ArrayController` (as the prior code's usage suggests), assigning a non-array `Group` object as its content/model is likely to break member rendering on the public group page.
